QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_54

question.text: Under SAS-1100 a 'housing unit delivered' output is simple; the OUTCOME indicator is:

answer.text: Sustained occupancy rate at 12 months + residents' self-reported quality-of-life score + reduction in housing-related expense

explanation.text: The Logic: Outcome is the CHANGE in well-being — sustained occupancy, quality-of-life score, reduction in repair expense (the Niwas case explicitly cites Rs. 10,000 annual saving). Unit count is output, not outcome. The Trap: Options A, B, D are output/aesthetic/spec indicators. Cross-Exam Context: Outcome-vs-output distinction echoed in XII Ch 1 and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: A simple 'repair-expense delta' Rs metric per family is audit-gold — the Chapter 8 Niwas case cites Rs. 10,000/year saved per family as a direct outcome.
